title: Retained mixture-trial training signal and realized exposure audit
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Retained metric suffixes and identity-resolved assignments can distinguish missing opponent turnover or update collapse from inconclusive strength evidence before further allocation.
material_change: Zero-new-hand descriptive suffix audit of all eight completed training stages, no model changes or causal claims.
notes: Prior current-pool audit diagnosed loss-kbest admission failure; this audit uses new anchor-latest mixture-trial data and resolves local slots to snapshot identities, without rerunning that old diagnosis.

result.summary: Eight retained training suffixes audited with zero new hands; stage2 observed84-86 recent snapshot IDs per branch, no obvious entropy collapse or update shutdown.
result.conclusion: Old pool admission failure no longer explains current result. Flat descriptive metrics do not prove convergence or causal critic/KL failure; repeated anchors and snapshot counts do not establish unseen strategic breadth.
result.decision: Do not patch KL or critic from descriptive loss trends. Prioritize one fixed training-pool-disjoint held-out opponent transfer check of all four retained endpoints and own parents.
result.next_step: Qualify held-out panel identities against pool provenance and preregister bounded fresh common-deck both-seat evaluation before outcomes, reusing qualified evaluator. No new Slumbot hands.
